name: Aptitude Test 02
subtitle: UVTN 2022 · Round 1: CV & Aptitude Test
description: Full-length simulation: 9 verbal reasoning, 10 quantitative reasoning (case exhibits) and 6 abstract reasoning questions in one 30-minute sitting, with no breaks between sections.
keyNote: The answer key follows the bolded options in the original test file; that file has no written explanations.

questions.intro: Eddie Chapman was an English criminal who became a spy for the Nazis during World War II. He was known to the Germans by the codename Fritz. However, he defected back to his home country and worked for many years as a double agent for the British. Chapman had been imprisoned on the Channel Islands when they fell into German hands. From there he was transferred to a French jail, where he became acquainted with Captain Stephan von Gröning, head of the Abwehr in Paris. Chapman offered von Gröning his services as a turncoat agent. After extensive training in explosives, radio communications and parachute jumping, Chapman was dropped into Cambridgeshire by the Germans on 16 December 1942. His mission was to sabotage the de Havilland aircraft factory in Hatfield. Instead, he surrendered to MI5. The sabotage was faked with their help in order to deceive the Germans. MI5 gave Eddie Chapman the codename Zigzag – a reference to the way he appeared to jump from one side to the other during the course of World War II. By 1944, Chapman was sent back to Britain by the Germans in order to report on the accuracy of the coordinates they were programming into their V1 weapon. Chapman repeatedly reported back to the Germans that the bombs fired by the weapon were hitting Central London. In fact, they were falling well short. Through this misinformation, the British were able to ensure that the wrong coordinates continued to be used and that bombs from the V1 fell in the countryside rather than their target in the heart of the capital. At the end of the war, Chapman received a £6,000 payment from MI5 and was allowed to keep £1,000 he had received from the Germans. He received no other money. He was granted a pardon for his pre-war activities. During the war, Chapman was also awarded the Iron Cross by the Germans for sabotaging the de Havilland aircraft factory.
questions.stem: Statement: Chapman received £7,000 at the end of the war.
Statement: The V1 weapon was not accurate.

Advertisement: Giant Furniture’s customers can expect high quality, competitive prices, and same-day delivery. Don’t buy a back-order slip somewhere else. Buy it today and we’ll deliver it tonight.
The reasoning behind the advertisement’s statement to not buy a back-order slip is to
options: guarantee the best deal in town.
advertise a promotional giveaway Giant Furniture is holding.
suggest that competitor furniture stores are not the same level.
distinguish itself from competitors by offering same-day delivery.
sell bedroom furniture in particular.

questions.stem:
The aeronautics commission recently released a report detailing a problem with the thrusters on the newly developed XR rocket. The rocket was designed to explore the near planets in the solar system but not within the orbit of the Moon. Federal regulations require the public to be alerted about any flaw in the design of spacecraft intended primarily to traverse space within the Moon’s orbit, but not further out in space. However, the aeronautics commission decided to release its report as soon as the flaw was discovered.
Which of the following, if true, most helps to explain the decision by the aeronautics commission?
options: The aeronautics commission has recently received negative publicity for a lack of transparency regarding craft design.

Until the government decided on the current regulations, the regulatory committee considered implementing stricter regulations that would require public disclosure of problems with any sort of spacecraft.
Spacecraft designed for traversing space solely within the orbit of the Moon have a greater likelihood of impacting the earth in the event of a problem.
The admission of a design flaw is not enough to deter the public from supporting future developments in space exploration technology.
Funding for future spacecraft might be affected if the flaws in the current rockets are made public.

questions.stem:
Hurricane Zach came ashore on the east coast of the United States in 1907. Another hurricane named Zach threatened islands off the coast of Florida in 1990. The National Hurricane Center has a policy of retiring names given to these storms so that no two storms could ever have the same name.
Which of the following, if true, best reconciles the discrepancy described above?
options: Hurricane Zach of 1907 came ashore in a different part of the country from the Zach of 1990.
In 1990, the hurricane center did not originally believe Zach would gain enough strength to become a hurricane.
Records of Hurricane Zach of 1907 indicate that Zach came ashore very late in the hurricane season.
The Hurricane Zach of 1990 was a category 4 hurricane.
The hurricane center first became aware of the 1907 Hurricane Zach when old weather records were discovered in 1995.

questions.stem:
Physiotherapist: Although the patient’s health would improve with daily outdoor walks, I have advised against it in the health plan. Since she is overweight, an increase in walking exercise would stress the already overstressed knee joints and would therefore put the patient at increased risk of injury.
The physiotherapist’s argument depends on which of the following?
options: The amount of exercise the patient currently undertakes does not put her at risk of joint injury.
Any patient is apt to be healthier with some exercise than with none at all
The patient will not attempt to take daily walks despite the recommendation of the physiotherapist.
The patient would use her knees during daily walks more than she currently does in other activities, such as bicycling.
The physiotherapist should have the patient’s best well-being as the foremost concern.

questions.stem:
A disease caused by a reproducing algae species has led to a substantial dwindle in the population of fish in one pond. If no measures are taken to rid the pond of these algae, all the fish in nearby ponds will die.
Which of the following, if true, would most damage the conclusion above?
options: Some of the algae in the contaminated pond will die before reproducing.
The species of fish in the pond produces waste containing bacteria that will destroy the algae before the algae can reach other ponds.
The species of algae in the pond is a favorite food of catfish.
There is no effective method of ridding the contaminated tank of algae.
All species of algae convert carbon dioxide to oxygen, a function vital to fish life.

questions.stem:
Psychologist: Negotiators who lie regularly to cover up mistakes or to form new business alliances know that “truth adherence” – the closeness with which a story aligns to the known facts, is more likely to win a listener’s trust than a completely unfamiliar story with corroboration from others. Clearly, people are more willing to trust a story that feels familiar but has a few inconsistencies, than a story that is entirely new but completely verifiable.
Which of the following most seriously calls into question the psychologist’s conclusion?
options: People are more likely to trust a negotiator if they have been referred by friends in common or trusted business acquaintances.
People tend not to become negotiators unless they already have a tendency to lie on a regular basis.
Most people who negotiate do lie once in a while, but only a very few do so regularly.
Although an entirely false story would immediately put the listener on guard, negotiators who are regular liars would never use such a tactic.
Negotiators who are regular liars are only slightly more likely than others to use stories that have “truth adherence” to form new business alliances.

questions.stem:
The energy policy of the United States has focused for years on developing methods of production, including nuclear power plants, and on increasing exploration for oil, gas, and coal. However, the country still faces energy shortages, and the environmental risks of most methods of energy production are increasingly unacceptable. It is clear that the United States must adopt a more realistic energy policy.
Which of the following policies would be most likely to lead to the resolution of the energy problems facing the United States as they are analyzed above?
options: Developing nuclear power plants that operate with fewer technicians.
Increasing the number of the country’s oil reserves that can be drawn on during times of shortage
Increasing the tax on energy consumption to encourage conservation.
Speeding construction and licensing approval of nuclear plants and other sources of cheaper power.
Encouraging energy use during off-peak hours to equalize the burden on existing power plants.

questions.stem:
In 2021, company A began producing instant cereal X and sold all of X produced. To make all of the instant cereal X in 2021, raw ingredients were hydrated until their weight was 40% less than their original weight, then a total of 30 kilograms of starch and spices were added just before X was packaged in cans. Did the company sell more than 4000 cans of X last year?
(1) Each can of instant cereal X sold last year contained 0.5 kilograms.
(2) Last year, the total weight of the raw ingredients for instant cereal X, before hydrating and excluding the starch and spices added after hydrating, was greater than 3,500 kilograms.

In the Micro Economics class, there were 150 students. The total number of lessons being taught was 20. Was the average (arithmetic mean) number of students attending each lesson greater than 100?
(1) Each student attended at least one lesson.
(2) The average number of lessons attended per student was greater than 12.
Which of the following statements is true?
options: On average, the export market excluding China is expected to grow at 50% per year or more
In 2019, the domestic market is expected to remain bigger than all export markets combined
Between 2016 and 2017, China’s market size is expected to increase 400% more than the export market excluding China
None of the above / we lack sufficient information at this stage

questions.stem: What would be the market size for farm heating systems in China in 2015, assuming that only natural gas (NG) heaters are sold?
Which piece of information is necessary to determine if Telyss will meet its 2015 target for China?
options: The profit margin per type of heater in 2015
The market share that would enable Telyss to break even in China in 2015
The share of Chinese customers who are willing to purchase a heater in 2015
The market share of Telyss in 2015 for China

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?
options: In China, the fuel cost is lower if heating with LPG instead of natural gas
In China, the electricity cost of heating with an electric heater is lower than the fuel cost of heating with LPG
In China, the fuel cost of heating with coal is not cheaper than the fuel cost of heating with LPG
In China, the electricity cost of heating with an electric heater is lower than the fuel cost of heating with coal

questions.stem: For each region, which type of heating system minimizes the heating cost per kWh?
options: North: electricity; South: coal; West: coal; East: coal
North: coal; South: NG; West: coal; East: electricity
North: coal; South: NG; West: NG; East: electricity
North: coal; South: LPG; West: NG; East: LPG

questions.stem: Which heater would you advise Telyss to sell in China? Your recommendation should match the objectives of the CEO.
options: The LPG heater
The natural gas heater
The electric heater
All three heaters
None of these three heaters can compete with coal heating

questions.stem: The price of natural gas is flexible and varies with market conditions. What is the maximum price per m3 for which using NG is cheaper or equal to using any other energies in all regions of China?
options: 2.00 CNY / m3
2.25 CNY / m3
2.50 CNY / m3
2.75 CNY / m3

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false?
options: In scenario 2, if the subcontractor copies Telyss’s product and sells it directly to customers, then there is a risk of increased competition
In scenario 2, if the subcontractor is not able to meet Telyss’s manufacturing standards, then there is a risk of decreased quality
In scenario 2, if the subcontractor goes bankrupt then there is a risk to business continuity
In both scenario 2 and scenario 3, the production is handled in China. As a result, there is no currency risk
